title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed federal law that establishes new rules for the development and deployment of artificial intelligence in the United States. It aims to promote safe, transparent, and accountable AI systems while protecting privacy, ensuring fairness, and fostering innovation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt to the construction of new data centers dedicated to AI workloads. The act aims to reduce environmental impacts, encourage sustainability, and allow for careful assessment of future AI infrastructure needs.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 aims to regulate the environmental footprint of AI systems, requiring developers to assess and mitigate energy consumption and resource use. The act establishes reporting requirements, sets carbon efficiency standards, and offers incentives for green AI technologies.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 prohibits artificial intelligence from diagnosing, treating, or prescribing medical care, ensuring that all patient interactions must involve a licensed human physician. It establishes strict regulations and penalties for medical practices that rely on AI for patient care, aiming to protect public health and maintain professional accountability.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The “Make AI Work for Americans Act” proposes policies to steer artificial‑intelligence development so it delivers clear benefits to U.S. citizens, focusing on job creation, economic growth, and public safety. It seeks to establish safeguards, incentives, and oversight that keep AI tools aligned with national interests and the well‑being of American communities.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a U.S. law that aims to give students from kindergarten through high school the knowledge and skills to understand and use artificial intelligence responsibly. It requires schools to add AI education to their curriculum, train teachers, and set guidelines to keep AI use safe, ethical, and fair for all learners.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 aims to make AI systems dependable and safe by setting clear standards for their development and deployment. It establishes guidelines for testing, transparency, and accountability so that AI technology can be trusted by the public and policymakers.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 aims to ensure that AI systems developed in the United States meet high standards of safety, transparency, and accountability. It establishes guidelines for researchers, funding priorities, and regulatory oversight to promote trustworthy and reliable AI technologies.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to launch a pilot program that uses artificial intelligence to protect critical infrastructure from cyber threats. It also sets out other related goals, though those specifics aren’t detailed here.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 establishes a framework for integrating artificial‑intelligence education into K‑12 curricula, ensuring students learn about AI concepts, ethics, and responsible use. It also requires schools to provide teacher training, instructional resources, and assessment tools so that students and educators are prepared for an increasingly AI‑centric world.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act aims to ensure that artificial‑intelligence systems used in processing veterans’ claims are transparent, fair, and reliable, setting clear standards for how data is handled and decisions are made. It also establishes oversight mechanisms and safeguards to protect veterans’ rights, promote accountability, and guarantee accurate, unbiased outcomes.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 is a law designed to make Virginia’s use of AI systems clear and accountable. It requires companies to openly explain how their AI models work, share data usage policies, and provide understandable reasons for any decisions that affect residents.

title: To establish age-appropriate design standards and safety safeguards for artificial intelligence chatbots accessed by minors, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This policy establishes design standards and safety safeguards that must be built into artificial intelligence chatbots so they are appropriate for minors to use. It also outlines additional safety measures for other contexts in which these chatbots might be accessed.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a nationwide framework for assessing and managing the risks posed by AI systems, requiring developers and users to conduct thorough risk evaluations before deployment. It also creates a federal oversight body that will set safety standards, enforce compliance, and review new AI technologies to protect public safety and privacy.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act would create a nationwide effort to help people understand what AI is and how it impacts everyday life. It would set up funding, partnerships, and educational programs so citizens can learn about AI safely and responsibly.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution establishes a Select Committee dedicated to Artificial Intelligence. It is intended to study AI-related issues and recommend policies to address them.

title: A bill to require the Secretary of Defense to establish reporting requirements and voluntary guidance for large artificial intelligence contractors.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The bill requires the Secretary of Defense to set up mandatory reporting requirements for large artificial intelligence contractors. It also encourages the establishment of voluntary guidance to help ensure these contractors operate responsibly and in line with defense goals.

title: A bill to provide for the retraining and support of workers displaced by automation technologies or artificial intelligence, to require Federal action during periods of elevated unemployment, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: This bill seeks to help workers displaced by automation and artificial intelligence by funding retraining and support programs. It also mandates federal action during periods of high unemployment to address the broader economic impacts of technology-driven job loss.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate’s resolution stresses the importance of protecting religious freedom as we develop and deploy artificial intelligence. It also urges that AI systems be transparent and guided by authoritative texts, ensuring that technology respects diverse beliefs and is open to scrutiny.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Safety Board, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes creating an Artificial Intelligence Safety Board to oversee and regulate AI development, ensuring it meets safety and ethical standards. It also includes additional measures related to AI policy and regulation, but the specific details are not provided.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a law designed to stop AI from tricking people into believing false or misleading information. It requires that AI systems be clearly labeled and that developers provide honest, transparent explanations about how the technology works so consumers can make informed choices.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy requires the Director of National Intelligence to provide Congress with a detailed report on how artificial intelligence systems are employed to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise handle information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. This report is intended to ensure congressional oversight and transparency of AI use in intelligence operations.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 aims to prepare workers for a future dominated by AI by updating educational curricula and training programs. It focuses on integrating AI literacy, reskilling initiatives, and partnerships between government, industry, and schools to ensure the workforce stays competitive and adaptable.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act is a legislative proposal that aims to promote open‑source development in artificial intelligence, encouraging collaboration and transparency. It seeks to establish guidelines and incentives for organizations to lead in open‑source AI initiatives, ensuring that AI technologies remain accessible and accountable.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 seeks to curb unfair pricing practices by AI companies and prevent them from setting artificially high or low prices for their services. It also aims to prohibit AI firms from colluding or using AI to manipulate wages, ensuring fair compensation for workers involved in AI-related work.

title: A bill to establish the Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill proposes creating a Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations to oversee and investigate issues related to cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. It also includes additional provisions for related regulatory and oversight purposes.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act is a law that aims to promote responsible use of artificial intelligence by requiring companies to provide clear information about how their AI models are built and how they operate. It mandates transparency about data sources, training methods, and potential biases so users can understand and evaluate the AI systems they interact with.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act is designed to shield households from rising utility bills driven by the high energy demand of AI data centers. It proposes rules to curb data‑center energy usage, encourage renewable sources, and limit the cost passed on to consumers.

title: Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act establishes a new government department to oversee AI and other emerging technologies. It outlines the department’s mission to advance research, regulate responsible use, and coordinate national efforts in AI development and deployment.
